_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING or UNREACHABLE for interp2d, each with the measurement or the proof behind it. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the claim and its reason live in one file, and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR -- every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. The FIRST scoring run of this unit declared NOTHING and scored 0.8072 with 32 survivors; it is committed as evidence/interp2d/mutation.first-run-nothing-declared.json -- kept OUT of mutation/ on purpose, because revcheck reads every result JSON under mutation/ as an artifact of the current instrument and a preserved older run reads there as a base-sha split, so what survived is on the record before any of it was excused. TEN are declared here and FOUR SURVIVORS ARE NOT -- the score is 0.987 and not 1.000, which is the point. READ THE SPLIT BEFORE THE SCORE. 17 of the original 32 are neither declared nor argued: they are KILLED, by ONE judgement in harness/ranges.toml (`nondecreasing_only`) rather than by seventeen more entries here. Of the ten declared, SIX are equivalences proved over the whole input structure and FOUR are UNREACHABLE-with-a-measurement, which is a weaker claim and is labelled as one on every entry. The four NOT declared are in evidence/interp2d/mutation.census.txt with the exact input that would kill each and the rule that does not exist to draw it.
98531180: compare_op '<' -> '<=' at `} else if (xq < xData[j - 1]) {`, the x-direction corner search. PROVED FROM THE LINE ABOVE IT, not from the input set. The immediately preceding arm of the same if/else chain is `if (xq == xData[j - 1]) { ... return ...; }`, so control reaches this test only when `xq != xData[j-1]`, and `<` and `<=` differ on exactly one input -- equality -- which this arm cannot see. The reference has the same shape (`IF (xq == xData(j)) ... ELSEIF (xq < xData(j))`), so this is a property of the transcription rather than of the translation. NaN does not open a gap: `xq` NaN returns at the function's first test, `xData(j)` NaN makes both spellings false. NOT REMOVED: the arm is the reference's, statement for statement.
143857a4: compare_op '<' -> '<=' at `} else if (yq < yData[i - 1]) {`, the y-direction corner search. The y half of 98531180, same proof one dimension over: the preceding arm is `if (yq == yData[i - 1]) { ... return ...; }`. The NaN half of that argument became true only at this dispatch -- until 7639168f this translation had no `std::isnan(yq)` guard, so a NaN `yq` DID reach this test and both spellings were false there anyway. The guard is now in (evidence/interp2d/yq-nan-guard.MISTRANSLATION.md), and a NaN `yq` returns before the loop.
7986e5f9: compare_op '<' -> '<=' at `if (x < xData_min) xData_min = x;`, the MINVAL reduction. THE SAME MUTANT, ON THE SAME FOUR LINES, AS interp1d's 20f2a843, and the proof transfers because both halves of it transfer. (i) The loop is byte-identical to interp1d's: seed DBL_MAX, `for (I = 1; I <= n; ++I)`, `if (x < min) min = x`. (ii) The consumer is the same predicate: interp2d reads `xData_min` at exactly one site, `if (xq <= xData_min || std::isnan(xq))`, and the added disjunct does not read it. Loosening the comparison DOES change the stored bits -- 1,666 of 69,905 swept tuples differ, because `-0.0 <= 0.0` is true where `-0.0 < 0.0` is false -- and it cannot change the CONSUMER, because IEEE says `+0.0 == -0.0`. evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.cpp sweeps every ordered tuple of length 0..4 over a 16-value set (both zeros, duplicates, both infinities, a NaN, DBL_MAX/MIN and their negatives) crossed with every query in the same set and reports 0 pairs whose consumer differs; re-run for THIS unit's four reductions and this unit's two consumers in evidence/interp2d/equivalence_probe.cpp / .txt. NOT REMOVED: the loop is gfortran's own MINVAL shape and `*std::min_element` disagrees with it under a NaN and on a zero-size array.
1235716b: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (x > xData_max) xData_max = x;`. The MAXVAL half of 7986e5f9, same probe, same run, same 0. Consumer is `} else if (xq >= xData_max) {`, the one site that reads it.
b9162232: compare_op '<' -> '<=' at `if (y < yData_min) yData_min = y;`. The y-direction MINVAL, same code and same argument as 7986e5f9. Consumer is `if (yq <= yData_min || std::isnan(yq))`. The four reductions are swept TOGETHER in one probe rather than separately, because a tie in one and a tie in another can occur in the same table and the question is whether the pair of consumers can see it.
acb38635: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (y > yData_max) yData_max = y;`. The y-direction MAXVAL. Consumer is `} else if (yq >= yData_max) {`.
f0949202: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` in `errmsg_trim`. EQUIVALENT ON EVERY VALUE OF THE TYPE, and the proof is two lines rather than a sweep: the two conditions differ at exactly one value, `n == 0`, and there the tight form takes `: 0` and yields 0 while the loose form takes `static_cast<size_t>(0)` and yields 0. Same length, same view, same string. For every other n the conditions agree. interp1d's b61327db is the same mutant at the same line of the same copied helper and was declared against an exhaustive sweep of all 4,294,967,296 int values reporting 0 differences (evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.txt); this entry states the reason that sweep found nothing. NOT REMOVED: a negative length is the view's NOT-ALLOCATED convention and the guard is what collapses it to the empty string rather than to a 4-billion-byte view.
98926651: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (static_cast<int>(s.size()) > ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)` in `assign_errmsg`. UNREACHABLE HERE, AND THAT IS A WEAKER CLAIM THAN EQUIVALENCE -- stated, not blurred. The two forms differ on exactly one input, `s.size() == n_ErrMsg_cap`. MEASURED over the corpus this unit's green was taken on: evidence/interp2d/errmsg_extremes_probe.cpp is the shipped translation with six counters and nothing else changed, run over the same 1147 cases -- `assign_errmsg calls 149`, `s.size(), min .. max 15 .. 42`, `n_ErrMsg_cap, min .. max 4099 .. 4103`, `calls with s.size() == cap 0`. The capacity is LEN(ErrMsg) + 4096 (harness/emit.py ALLOC_HEADROOM) in the differential harness and the same 4096 in the integrated build (vit_errorvariables_view.f90), and this unit's longest message is 42 bytes, so the guard is true by a margin of four thousand in every configuration this campaign can build. FIFTH UNIT AT THIS SITE with this reason -- ReadAvrSWAP e82a5f90, ExtController 11d2c9cc, UpdateZeroMQ ac7a5b72, interp1d e34d5cc4 -- and the reason has not changed. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a byte comparison cannot catch.
34ae41de: const_tweak '1' -> '2' at `ErrVar->aviFAIL = -1;` in the `SIZE(xData) != SIZE(zData,2)` branch. UNREACHABLE BY A STATED DOMAIN JUDGEMENT, not by an accident of the draws, and the judgement is measured. `harness/ranges.toml` ties n_zData_cols to n_xData because the reference has NO ANSWER when they differ: its branch is `ErrVar%aviFAIL = -1` followed by an internal WRITE that formats 59 characters into `ErrVar%ErrMsg` AS IT STANDS, with no literal assignment in front of it to lengthen the record. Measured in isolation at LEN(ErrMsg) = 0: 'Fortran runtime error: End of record', exit 2 (evidence/interp2d/reference.size-mismatch-aborts.txt), and the corpus's own ErrMsg lengths are 1..12, all far short of 59. So on every input that enters this branch the oracle ENDS THE PROCESS, and no differential instrument can grade a mutant inside it. THE TIE IS NOT FREE AND IS NOT HIDDEN: it is reported in the run, it lands in harness/interp2d.json as `tied_extents`, and what it costs is exactly this mutant and its y-direction twin. WHAT IS NOT GIVEN UP is the property the tie was chosen to protect: n_zData_rows follows n_yData and n_zData_cols follows n_xData, tied to DIFFERENT partners, so the two extents stay distinct from each other and a translation that strode this column-major array by the column count still disagrees on every case.
bc897a8f: const_tweak '1' -> '2' at `ErrVar->aviFAIL = -1;` in the `SIZE(yData) != SIZE(zData,1)` branch. The y half of 34ae41de: same branch shape, same 59-character WRITE, same tie, same measurement. Declared as one claim made twice rather than as two claims, and if the tie is ever lifted both come back together.
